summary: A guide to using Telnet to reach UCSB's Online System. It explains why and how the system was connected, its limitations, the virtual keyboard, and local commands such as help, prefix, shift, duplex mode and logout. It includes examples of logging on and instructing the user Telnet program.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how a Network user could operate UCSB's Online System from a remote terminal. It describes special key names, local commands, output limits, and example sessions.

subtitle: A guide to using a text terminal to access UCSB's Online System through TELNET.

tldr.problem: UCSB's Online System used a specialized keyboard and display, while Network users connected through TELNET with a virtual teletype.
tldr.mechanism: NETOLS maps TELNET characters to Online System keys, offers commands for special keys and connection settings, and converts system output for the remote user.
tldr.outcome: The RFC explains access, keyboard mappings, commands, display changes, and examples. It also documents functions that do not work in the TELNET environment.

sections.title: Network Access to OLS
sections.content:
RFC 216 describes NETOLS, a Network front end that lets TELNET users reach UCSB's Online System (OLS). OLS was designed for a specialized double keyboard and had graphical display features, so NETOLS translates between TELNET input and the OLS interface.

The document is a guide to the Network interface, not a general user's manual for OLS.
sections.plainLanguage: NETOLS acts as an interpreter between a remote terminal and OLS. The guide explains this interface rather than teaching every part of OLS.

sections.title: The Virtual OLS Keyboard
sections.content:
Many lower-keyboard keys map one-to-one from TELNET characters. Other keys, including all upper-keyboard keys, are entered by typing a prefix, a key name or unique abbreviation, and a space.

The default prefix is semicolon. Typing it twice sends the semicolon as ordinary input, and the PREFIX command can change it to another permitted character.
sections.plainLanguage: Type common characters directly. To press a special OLS key, type the prefix, its name, and a space.

sections.title: Commands and Display Limits
sections.content:
NETOLS provides HELP, PREFIX, SHIFT, UNSHIFT, FULLDUPLEX, HALFDUPLEX, STATE, and LOGOUT commands. They control key lookup, character mapping, echo, connection state, and logout.

OLS graphics and user-created special characters are suppressed in this TELNET interface. Greek characters are shown as lowercase letters, and tools that depend on a fixed screen may behave differently on a scrolling terminal.
sections.plainLanguage: Commands can change the prefix, echo, and letter mapping. Graphics and some screen-based features do not pass through this text interface.
